intentAndPurpose.intent: Accessible tabbed navigation on Base UI Tabs. Figma node 1:55592: inactive labels use content/low (`--Text-Low`), selected labels use content/high (`--Text-High`), accent is the indicator bar only (`--Primary-Tinted` / colour/content/tinted). Not TintedA11y on labels.

props.description: Appearance forwarded to all child TabItems.

interactionBehavior.summary: Tabs are Base UI tabs with OneUI chrome on top: hover and press recolour the label and slots only — the state-layer stay transparent in every state, and the selected bar is a single list-level indicator that slides between tabs rather than a per-tab underline. Default activation is manual: arrow keys move focus without changing the selected tab; `Enter` / `Space` commit. Pass `activateOnFocus` to make arrows select immediately.
hover: Only an unselected tab changes on hover: the label steps to `--Neutral-High` (overridable via `--Tabs-colorHover`) and the start / end slots step to `--Neutral-Tinted`.
The padded state-layer stays `transparent` — there is no hover fill and the selected indicator does not appear under an unselected tab.
Wrapped in `@media (hover: hover)`, so a touch tap never leaves a stuck hover colour behind.
Selected tabs (`[data-active]`) and disabled tabs are excluded from every hover rule, so the selected label already at `--Neutral-High` does not flicker.
press: An unselected press drops the label and both slots to `--Neutral-Low` (overridable via `--Tabs-colorPressed` / `--Tabs-iconColorPressed`).
Press is NOT `(hover: hover)`-guarded, so a touch tap gets the same colour drop a mouse press does.

The start-slot icon scales UP to `1.14` while the tab is held — the label and end slot do not move. This selector does not exclude `[data-active]`, so a selected tab with a start icon still grows on press. This is opposite to Button, which scales the whole control DOWN.
Selected tabs are excluded from press colour (`:not([data-active])`), so the already-active label does not drop to `--Neutral-Low`.
focus: Keyboard focus draws the two-layer halo on the inner state-layer, not the tab button: an inner `--Stroke-XL` gap ring in `--Surface-Halo-Gap` plus an outer `--Focus-Outline` ring, so it stays legible inside a tinted `<Surface>`.
`:focus` on the tab only clears the native outline; the visible ring is `:focus-visible`, so a mouse click does not paint it.
The panel uses a simpler `outline` in `--Focus-Outline` at `--Focus-Outline-Width` when it is itself `:focus-visible` — it does not use the two-layer halo.
keyboard: Default `activateOnFocus={false}`: `ArrowRight` / `ArrowLeft` (horizontal) or `ArrowDown` / `ArrowUp` (vertical) move focus only — the previously selected tab stays selected until `Enter` or `Space`.
`activateOnFocus` flips that: the same arrows both move focus and select immediately (Base UI automatic activation).
`Home` / `End` jump focus to the first / last tab. `loopFocus` defaults to `true`, so arrows wrap at the ends.

Disabled tabs stay in the arrow path: Base UI Tabs marks them `aria-disabled` with `focusableWhenDisabled`, and the list passes an empty `disabledIndices` array, so arrows land on them. They still refuse `Enter` / `Space` / click.
A value change also smooth-scrolls the selected tab into the overflowing list viewport, without using `scrollIntoView` (that would scroll ancestor pages).
selected: The selected tab's label is `--Neutral-High` and its start / end slots switch to `--{Role}-Tinted` — label stays Neutral; only the icon takes the appearance role.
Font weight stays `--Label-FontWeight-Medium` when selected, so the row does not shift as tabs activate.

The selected bar is a list-level indicator in `--{Role}-Tinted` (overridable via `--Tabs-indicatorColor`). It tracks Base UI's `--active-tab-*` vars and is inset by the state-layer padding so it underlines the content, not the padded tab.
Horizontal: a bottom bar of `--Stroke-XL` thickness. Vertical: a left bar whose height is centred in the active tab.
Selected is exposed as `aria-selected` and `[data-active]` by Base UI.
disabled: A disabled tab dims to `--Disabled-Opacity` and recolours the label to `--Primary-Low`.

Base UI keeps it `aria-disabled` rather than natively `disabled`, so it remains focusable and `cursor: not-allowed` on the tab is actually observable — unlike Button, there is no `pointer-events: none`.
Hover and press colour, and the start-slot press scale, are all suppressed via `:not([data-disabled])`.
Click, `Enter`, and `Space` do not activate it; tests confirm `aria-selected` stays `false`.
touch: On touch-only devices the hover colour never applies; the pressed `--Neutral-Low` label plus the start-slot scale-up are the entire tap response.
Pointer-move hover tracking is not used — unlike SegmentedControl, Tabs has no sliding hover pill.
